data.title: Mebendazole
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antiparasitics_

**Class:** Benzimidazole anthelmintic

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits parasite microtubule (β-tubulin) polymerisation → impaired glucose uptake → worm death

## Pharmacokinetics
- Very poorly absorbed (<10%) — mainly acts in the gut lumen

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Intestinal worms (pinworm, roundworm, hookworm, whipworm)
- Cutaneous larva migrans (less effective than albendazole — poor absorption)
- Trichinosis (with steroids), hydatid disease (high doses, historical)

## Dose & formulations
- 100 mg twice daily × 3 days, or 500 mg single dose; pinworm 100 mg single, repeat after 2 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Abdominal pain, diarrhoea; with high doses — neutropenia, hepatitis, alopecia
- SJS/TEN reported when combined with metronidazole

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy (first trimester); children under 1 year

## Drug interactions
- Metronidazole: SJS/TEN reports; cimetidine raises levels; carbamazepine lowers them

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid in the first trimester.

## Viva points
- Poorly absorbed — luminal worms; albendazole preferred for tissue parasites like CLM

_Sources: Khopkar ch.5; Wolverton 4e ch.12. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
